title: Supplemental insurance
summary: Overview of UnitedHealthcare supplemental plans, including dental, vision, fixed benefit, accident, critical illness, hospital, travel and term life coverage.

assets.alt: Illustration for dental and vision plans

atoms.title: What supplemental health insurance is
atoms.question: What is supplemental insurance?
atoms.text: Supplemental health insurance provides help with, or supplements, a health plan by providing additional benefits that can help with out-of-pocket expenses such as deductibles, coinsurance and copays, or even cover routine dental or vision products. UnitedHealthcare notes that a medical insurance plan is not going to cover everything, so completing coverage with supplemental plans can help protect against unexpected costs.

atoms.title: Who underwrites UnitedHealthcare supplemental plans
atoms.question: Who provides UnitedHealthcare supplemental insurance plans?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare's supplemental plans, such as dental, vision or fixed benefit health insurance plans, can help cover medical expenses not covered by a medical plan. These plans are underwritten by Golden Rule Insurance Company, a UnitedHealthcare company, and help round out other health insurance coverage. Shoppers can enter a ZIP code to find a plan or call 1-855-972-1023 (TTY 711).

atoms.title: Dental insurance versus dental savings memberships
atoms.question: What is the difference between dental insurance and a dental savings membership?
atoms.text: Dental insurance plans offer coverage for many common dental care services. Dental savings memberships are an alternative to insurance that helps people save on qualified services from participating providers. UnitedHealthcare states that dental discount memberships are not insurance.

atoms.title: What vision insurance helps cover
atoms.question: What does vision insurance help pay for?
atoms.text: Vision insurance plans can help people cover and budget for vision care expenses such as routine eye exams, prescription glasses and/or contact lenses. UnitedHealthcare lists vision insurance among its supplemental options alongside dental insurance and fixed benefit health insurance.

atoms.title: Fixed benefit health insurance overview
atoms.question: What is fixed benefit health insurance?
atoms.text: Fixed indemnity insurance, also marketed as fixed benefit health insurance, is meant to help ease some common hospital and doctor out-of-pocket costs with cash benefits paid for qualified medical services. UnitedHealthcare states that the product provides limited benefits, is a supplement to health insurance, and is not a substitute for the minimum essential coverage required by the Affordable Care Act (ACA).

Is fixed benefit insurance a replacement for major medical coverage?

atoms.title: Limited-benefit warning for fixed indemnity products
atoms.question: Does a fixed indemnity plan satisfy ACA minimum essential coverage?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare states that fixed indemnity products provide limited benefits and are a supplement to health insurance, not a substitute for the minimum essential coverage required by the Affordable Care Act. Lack of major medical coverage or other minimum essential coverage may result in an additional payment with taxes. These products pay benefits in a stated amount regardless of the actual expenses incurred, and not all plans on the page are fixed benefit plans.

atoms.title: More supplemental options beyond dental and vision
atoms.question: What other supplemental plans does UnitedHealthcare offer?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare lists several more options: accident insurance helps with costs of qualifying accidental injuries and pays regardless of other coverage; critical illness insurance pays lump sum cash benefits for qualifying serious illnesses; hospital insurance pays a fixed cash amount per day for hospital stays; international travel insurance covers medical emergencies, lost passports or baggage and travel assistance; term life insurance pays beneficiaries a lump sum on death; and mental health virtual therapy is offered for one monthly cost.

atoms.title: Why combine supplemental plans
atoms.question: Why combine insurance plans and non-insurance health products?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare says combining insurance plans and non-insurance health products is a way to build a mix of healthcare options that meet a person's needs. A shopper could also save money compared to buying the plans individually.

atoms.title: Three reasons to choose supplemental insurance
atoms.question: Why choose supplemental insurance?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare gives three reasons to consider supplemental plans. Get complete coverage: fill gaps with help paying out-of-pocket costs not covered by a regular medical plan. Protect your finances: cash benefit plans that pay a lump sum can give peace of mind if a critical illness or accident happens. Customize for your needs: with a variety of plans, shoppers can match coverage to their age, family and situation.

How can supplemental plans protect my finances?

atoms.title: Is supplemental insurance worth buying
atoms.question: Is it worth it to buy supplemental insurance?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare says that because supplemental plans cover many different needs, a person may decide one or more is definitely worth the price for themselves and their family. The page frames supplemental plans as a way to help protect a person and their family when something major happens to their health.

atoms.title: Dental and vision in Medicare, Medicaid, employer plans
atoms.question: Do Medicare, Medicaid or employer plans include dental and vision?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare points out that dental, vision and supplemental coverage may be included with some Medicare plans, like Medicare Advantage or Medicare Supplement (Medigap) plans. Dental, vision and other extra benefits are included with some, but not all, Medicaid plans. Employers can also offer specialty plans such as dental, vision and supplemental options to give employees added benefits.
